name: Jeep Wrangler
evaluation_notes: JK (2012–2018) or JL (2018+) generation. Avoid 2007–2011 JK with the 3.8L engine (underpowered, more issues) — 2012+ Pentastar 3.6L is the right engine. Buyer wants a capable, reliable off-road vehicle — not a project, not a daily driver. Clean title essential. JK sweet spot: 2014–2018, 60k–110k miles, $13k–$20k. JL sweet spot: 2018–2021, 50k–100k miles, $18k–$25k. Reward: Rubicon trim (locking diffs, sway bar disconnect), Pentastar 3.6L, documented service history, factory or mild lift only. Penalize: heavily lifted examples (suspension stress, death wobble risk), evidence of off-road abuse without maintenance, automatic with towing damage. Flag: death wobble mentions, rust on tub floor or rockers, soft top damage.

name: Jeep Gladiator
evaluation_notes: 2020+ only (JT generation, the only generation). Shares the JL Wrangler platform and Pentastar 3.6L drivetrain with a mid-size truck bed — excellent capability plus utility. Buyer is not shopping for a daily driver. Rubicon trim strongly preferred (locking front and rear diffs, disconnecting sway bar). Sport S and Overland acceptable at the right price. Sweet spot: 2020–2022, under 70k miles, $22k–$30k. Reward: Rubicon trim, factory tow package, hard top, low miles for year. Penalize: Mojave trim (desert-tuned suspension, not optimal for rock crawling), near-MSRP pricing, heavily modified examples. Flag: frame rust, accident history, death wobble.

name: Toyota 4Runner
evaluation_notes: 5th gen only (2014+). Most reliable SUV on this list — 1GR-FE V6 runs forever with basic maintenance, timing chain not belt. TRD Off Road or TRD Pro trim preferred (KDSS suspension, locking rear diff). SR5 4WD is acceptable. Sweet spot: 2015–2020, 70k–130k miles, $18k–$30k. Reward: TRD Off Road/Pro trim, KDSS equipped, documented Toyota dealer service history. Penalize: 2WD models, near-MSRP on recent years, SR5 without locking rear diff. Flag: no service history, rust in northern-climate vehicles, accident damage.

name: Lexus GX460
evaluation_notes: 2014+ only (post-interior refresh). Same platform and 4.6L V8 as the 4Runner but with a luxury interior and KDSS standard on all trims — outstanding off-road capability with a comfortable cabin. Best value luxury overlander available. Sweet spot: 2015–2019, 60k–110k miles, $18k–$30k. Reward: full service history, low miles for year, KDSS (standard 2014+), Premium trim or above. Penalize: accident history, deferred maintenance signs, near-MSRP on recent years. Note: 2017+ shows the best depreciation curve for buyers.

name: Toyota FJ Cruiser
evaluation_notes: All years 2007–2014 (discontinued after 2014). Same proven 4.0L 1GR-FE V6 and 4WD system as the 4Runner — extremely reliable, cult following keeps values stable. TRD package preferred (locking rear diff, skid plates). Poor rear visibility is a known design quirk, not a defect. Sweet spot: 2010–2014, 80k–140k miles, $13k–$20k. Reward: TRD package with locking rear diff, documented service history, low miles for year, rust-free southern or western state vehicle. Penalize: rust on frame or wheel wells (these rust badly in northern/salt climates — check undercarriage carefully), heavily lifted examples, unknown modification history. Flag: frame rust, transmission slipping, no service records. Hold to a high value standard — only surface as a deal if price is genuinely below market.
